trust_decision.summary: Whether a copy dereferences a symbolic link (reading bytes from outside the source tree) or recreates the link, decided per source path in NodeHfsImpl.copy() and per directory entry in NodeHfsImpl.copyAll()'s list() loop.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'recursive copy follows symlinked files', so the first place an engineer looks is the copyAll() loop that decides 'directory -> recurse, else -> copy()' from a Dirent list without ever consulting entry.isSymlink.

fix_sites.entry_point: hfs.copy(source, destination) / NodeHfsImpl#copy, exported by @humanfs/node (packages/node/src/index.js:6) and reached through Hfs#copy (packages/core/src/hfs.js:649-653)
hfs.copyAll(source, destination) / NodeHfsImpl#copyAll, reached through Hfs#copyAll (packages/core/src/hfs.js:664-668)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/deno/src/deno-hfs.js:298-300 (DenoHfsImpl#copy delegates straight to deno.copyFile) and packages/deno/src/deno-hfs.js:311-338 (DenoHfsImpl#copyAll repeats the same 'if (entry.isDirectory) recurse else copy' loop with no isSymlink branch; its list() at packages/deno/src/deno-hfs.js:246-248 yields raw deno.readDir entries), and packages/deno/src/deno.d.ts:7-24 declares none of readDir/lstat/readLink/symlink, so a Deno fix also needs the type shim

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Deno adapter lives in a separate package with its own test runner, and the report plus the published fix are about the Node fs.copyFile path, so a solver can call the Deno impl another runtime's problem rather than the same bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A copied tree must still contain a working link: the fix recreates each symlink with its original target text (the fix asserts the destination link target equals the source target, fix.diff:84-85), and regular files/directories must still copy byte-for-byte and recursively; an over-broad fix that resolves link targets to absolute paths, rewrites them relative to the destination, or drops/throws on link entries breaks legitimate in-tree links and loses entries from the copy.

O6_input_shapes: copy() where the source is a symlink to a file (string path)
copy() where the source is a symlink to a file (file URL)
copyAll() where the source is a symlink to a file, routed through copy() via the isFile() check
copyAll() where a nested entry is a symlink to a file
copyAll() where a nested entry is a symlink to a directory
copyAll() where the symlink sits at any depth in the recursive walk

O7_producer.where: packages/node/src/node-hfs.js:69-74 (NodeHfsDirectoryEntry constructor maps Dirent.isSymbolicLink() into entry.isSymlink; list() at packages/node/src/node-hfs.js:303-311 yields these entries)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: copyAll() whose top-level source argument is itself a symlink to a directory: isFile() uses stat (follows the link) so it returns false, then createDirectory() plus list() readdir through the link and the whole external tree is copied recursively
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The caller passed the source path explicitly, so following it looks like ordinary cp semantics; the advisory example and the published fix only inspect entries found inside the tree.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the landing point, two lines above the loop

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a moveAll() cross-device (EXDEV) fallback implemented as copyAll() + deleteAll()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: docs/decisions.md:73 already states that moveAll() 'may need to fall back to calling copyAll() and deleteAll()', so a maintainer adding that fallback would route every move through the unfixed sink and need the same lstat/isSymlink rule.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an options argument on copy()/copyAll() (for example { dereference: true } or { verbatimSymlinks }) mirroring fs.cp
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: These two methods are the only ones in this adapter with no options object, while node:fs/promises cp exposes dereference/verbatimSymlinks; copying that surface would add a second branch that decides whether to follow the link.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a link object kind in the in-memory volume, with copyObject() deciding whether to clone the link or its target
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MemoryHfsVolume already models objects, kinds and a clone path (copyObject) and hard-codes isSymlink:false at packages/memory/src/memory-hfs-volume.js:581; adding a link kind is a small, natural extension that reintroduces the same choice.

O9_family: path traversal via symlink following (CWE-22, link resolution / CWE-59)

O10_build.toolchain: npm workspaces; per-package tsc build run by pretest; mocha for packages/node; deno test for packages/deno; eslint/prettier
O10_build.project_tests: packages/node/tests/node-hfs.test.js runs the shared HfsImplTester (packages/test/src/hfs-impl-tester.js:994-1180, which already covers copy() and copyAll() for regular files and directories) plus package-specific cases; it ends at packages/node/tests/node-hfs.test.js:259 with no symlink coverage at the pinned commit, so the fix's own copy()/copyAll() symlink tests (fix.diff:52-133) are new.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the recursive loop (for example `if (entry.isSymlink) continue;` in copyAll), which stops the demonstrated leak but silently drops entries and leaves Hfs.copy() dereferencing a symlink source.

out_of_scope_notes: copyAll() also writes into an existing destination path without an lstat guard, so a symlinked destination entry could redirect the write; that is outside the advisory's source-tree property and was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb: no shell was available to measure the checkout; the source tree is roughly 40 JS/TS files across 8 packages, so tiny_repo is inferred from the file listing, not measured.
present_in_latest: the inputs give no latest release ('none'), so whether the O8 route is still open today is unknown.

Deno testability: DenoHfsImpl takes its deno object as a constructor option so it can be driven from Node with a stub, but packages/deno/src/deno.d.ts:7-24 declares no readDir/lstat/readLink and packages/deno/package.json:22 runs the real deno binary, which was neither installed nor exercised here.
The full advisory text was not available beyond the supplied summary; whether it names the Deno adapter explicitly is unknown.
